Vaccines with this element kept making protein under stress and matched or exceeded current vaccines in immune response, without costly modified nucleotides. The piece presents viral translation tricks as a possible path to cheaper and hardier RNA medicines.
pmc-13264228:
Long Bai and Jia-Can Su propose rethinking pain control during bone healing in a 2026 article on nerve and skeleton units. Fracture repair unfolds through clotting, inflammation, vessel remodeling and callus hardening, and the bone coverings are richly wired with sensory nerves. Those nerves do more than report pain; recent mapping work shows the same fibers send growth instructions that repair requires to proceed on schedule.

Lasting pain involves nerve circuits stuck in an alarm state, amplified by channels that boost excitability. Simply silencing all sensation could therefore slow healing, while ignoring pain leaves harmful plasticity in place. Smart analgesia, as framed here, means blocking pathological pain signals selectively while preserving helpful sensory input. The concept reframes dosing choices after fractures.
pmc-13264328:
Louise Cai and colleagues question liver stiffness testing in Fontan heart patients in a 2026 retrospective analysis. The Fontan operation reroutes blood flow for people born with one working heart chamber, but liver congestion and scarring follow over time. Sixty-five adults at one hospital contributed records and over one hundred stiffness scans across a decade. The team tracked whether stiffness changed with years since surgery. They also tested whether stiffness predicted decompensation or cancer review triggers.

Stiffness did not shift significantly between consecutive decades after surgery. Only two ultrasound heart measures tracked with stiffness scores. A derived portal hypertension outcome aligned with several blood test changes instead. Routine stiffness numbers alone may mislead surveillance, so combined clinical and laboratory judgment remains important for this growing adult group.
pmc-13264428:
Sarvesh P Azgaonkar led a 2026 case report on a giant cystic neck tumor in a man in his 90s. The growth was a very rare skin gland cancer with a long name, SCACP for short. Such tumors can look like harmless cysts, which makes them hard to name and treat.

The swelling had grown for two years and filled the left half of his neck. A needle test gave no clear answer, and scans showed spread across both front and back parts of the neck. Surgeons removed it through the neck, and lab tests with three markers confirmed the rare cancer. The authors stress lab study of the tissue as the way to tell this growth from common cysts.
pmc-13264628:
Eman AbdElRhiem and colleagues wrote a 2026 chemistry study on slowing rust-like damage to brass in salty water. They used a sulfur compound called MBT, a known protective agent, plus tiny particles of two oxides. The question was which particle partner makes the protective film work best.

In salt water like seawater, MBT alone reached 97.4 percent protection at its best dose. Adding titanium oxide particles lifted protection to 98.2 percent, while silica particles gave 94 percent, below MBT alone at that dose. Tests showed MBT sticks to the brass surface on its own, forming a film. Computer models said the titanium partner binds most strongly and passes charge best. The authors credit the particle's electronic nature, not a simple barrier effect, for the gain.
pmc-13264728:
Lili Luo, Shulian Li and Qiang Ji build an interpretable prediction model for young women with an aggressive breast cancer form in a 2026 study. Triple-negative invasive ductal cancer in women aged twenty to forty spreads readily and carries poor outlook. A feature selection plus modeling pipeline used it, explained with contribution analysis.

pmc-13264928:
Sanxiu He and a large team published a 2026 study on a protein that helps a common lymphoma dodge the immune system. The cancer is diffuse large B-cell lymphoma, and up to 40 percent of patients relapse or resist standard therapy. The protein, HMGB2, is overproduced in this cancer, but its role was unclear.

Cancer cells ship HMGB2 out in tiny bubbles, and it switches macrophages, immune cells in the tumor, into a calm state that eats fewer cancer cells. Blocking that chain restored macrophage eating and boosted a standard antibody drug. The authors name the chain as a drug target.
pmc-13265428:
Eleonora Pagan, Chukwuma Okoye, Luca Cuffaro, and a wider team wrote this systematic review, published in 2026. It pools trials of multidomain programs for older adults, packages that train body, mind, and diet together, to see what they do for health.

The review covered thirty-eight studies in people aged sixty and up without major dementia, lasting two months to three years. Every program included exercise; most added cognitive and nutritional parts, and many added more. Physical performance improved clearly, and frailty scores eased. The analysis also tracked thinking and mood outcomes with standard statistical pooling. The authors say combined programs beat single-fix thinking for aging well. The open question is which ingredients and doses matter most, since programs varied widely across the trials pooled.
pmc-13266128:
Laura Magaly Charlanne and colleagues study huddling and food effects on energy saving in young garden dormice, published in 2026. Late-born juveniles must grow, fatten, and prepare for first winter under changing conditions. Torpor and group huddling both save energy. Housing and feeding conditions were varied before hibernation.

Huddling changed torpor patterns and food intake during preparation. Despite those differences, juveniles reached similar size and weight at hibernation start and end. Food availability during hibernation altered total energy use, especially in males. The authors link that gap to reproductive investment. pmc-13266228:
Natali Shirron and the team systematically review fertility results after treatment for non-breast solid cancers in young adults (2026). Early-onset cancer is rising while parenthood is delayed. A total of 102 studies were kept, mixing case reports with analytical studies. Results covered ovarian failure, menses return, sperm recovery, hormones, pregnancy, and live birth. Two reviewers screened and extracted independently. Variation between studies forced synthesis. The review maps gonadal risks to guide preservation counselling.
pmc-13266928:
Jennifer Bou Zeid and co-authors published a research paper in 2026 on molecular cages whose shape can be reprogrammed by changing a building block's oxidation state. Cages assembled from metal ions and organic linkers can trap guests, but normally their form is fixed at synthesis. The team's linker carries an electron-rich unit that oxidizes cleanly.

In its normal state, four linkers and two palladium ions form a cage that selectively binds medium-length dinitrile guests. Oxidized, the same parts assemble into a smaller cage, and mixing in a second linker yields a mixed cage that can pair into a large four-metal assembly. Reducing reverses the sequence. pmc-13267128:
Zhaojing Wang, Linlin Wang, and Shicheng Zhang review in 2026 how pairs of class A G protein-coupled receptors can work as dimers in mental disorders. These receptors form the largest family of drug targets, and most sit in the brain, shaping mood, thought, and behavior. When two receptors pair, their signaling can differ sharply from either one acting alone.

It then analyzes the known structures of receptor pairs to explain how they assemble and switch on. Current attempts to design drugs that hit only a specific pair are assessed, offering a framework for more precise mental health medicines.
pmc-13267428:
Muhamed Baljevic and colleagues wrote a 2026 study of how suspected heart amyloidosis is worked up in United States practice. In this disease, stiff protein deposits build up in the heart. Two main types need different treatments, so sorting them fast and correctly matters. The team read electronic health records from 2017 to 2023.

They tracked three patient groups: about 1,650 with one type, about 1,050 with the other, and 59 with signs of both. Only about half to two-thirds got any targeted test within two years before diagnosis. Full protein testing, a key step, was done in well under half of each group. pmc-13267528:
Kapoor and Kabir grade two-stage hip swaps for germ-hit half swaps in this twenty twenty-six study. A half swap fights a worn hip with a ball on a post in the thigh. Germ in that joint is grim and hard to clear in one cut.

Hip scores leapt from a low base to a sound band at last check. Germ cleared in all but one of the two dozen sick folks. Half walked free of aids, and no swap slipped or shook loose.
pmc-13267628:
Yunli Li and a large team report a 2026 survey of a cat virus in captive giant pandas in China. Feline panleukopenia virus attacks meat-eating animals and can spill into rare species. About 57 percent of samples tested positive, and levels stayed high across the years. Young pandas and summer samples showed lower rates, which the team links to mother's antibodies and weaker virus survival in summer. Pandas with a past transfer between sites trended toward higher risk. Current vaccines seemed to raise weak responses. The authors urge tailored vaccines, tighter hygiene in risky seasons, and care with animal transfers.
pmc-13267928:
Shih-Chieh Lo and colleagues present a 2026 study of jaw-advancing mouthpieces for sleep apnea, watched during sleep endoscopy. These devices hold the lower jaw forward to keep the throat open. The advanced device cleared full blockage at the soft palate in about 35 percent of cases where the standard one had not. It cleared blockage at the voice box flap in 80 percent during head turning. The authors call this a trade-off needing longer study.
pmc-13269028:
Sayed Mortaza Fayez wrote a review article in 2026 surveying where nanomedicine, medicine built at a tiny scale, stands. The review looks at recent clinical gains, at blocks that slow new treatments, and at what may come next. Worked examples with numbers are used to show broad trends.

Those examples include 23 studies with 412 patients on uneven drug spread in tumors, and 847 clinical trials listed from 2010 to 2020. pmc-13269928:
Vikas Kumar Kushwaha and co-authors published a physics paper in 2026 simulating one active particle, an intruder, moving through a dense crowd of self-steering active particles. pmc-13270228:

Two of the new species differ from the genus's type species in the front of the head capsule, so their placement is marked as provisional. pmc-13270428:

pmc-13271128:

pmc-13271328:

pmc-13271428:

pmc-13271828:

pmc-13271928:

pmc-13272028:

Thousands developed depression over follow-ups of two to eight years, at rates that differed by country. Frailty scores were modeled against that risk with several survival methods. Grip strength was tested as a middle step that might carry part of the effect.
pmc-13272128:

pmc-13273128:

pmc-13273828:

pmc-13274128:

pmc-13274928:

pmc-13275628:

pmc-13276128: Jonna Hybelius and co-authors published a study of basic emotions in people with persistent physical symptoms receiving exposure therapy or lifestyle promotion in primary care. Their 2026 correction notice fixes errors in a paragraph on how stable emotion questionnaire answers were over time. The emotion surprise had wrong stability figures, and figures for shame were left out of a summary range. The corrected text reports surprise as far less stable than the other emotions and notes the team dropped it from later analysis. The original article has been corrected.
pmc-13276328:

On a dataset of more than 440,000 images, in-domain accuracy topped ninety percent for both tasks. Performance held up respectably on unseen categories, which suits real farm scouting.
pmc-13276428:

The network predicts temperature, relative humidity, and airborne dust at fine detail across space and time. It beat conventional graph models in the team's experiments. Analyzing the extra inputs showed each contributed differently to the three forecasts. The authors aim to support day-to-day operations and maintenance planning at sandy solar stations.
pmc-13276528:

pmc-13278928:
Mariano Reynoso and co-authors reanalyse preeclampsia, aspirin, and birthweight data in a 2026 paper.
